lesson.title: Llevar + Time Expressions
lesson.subtitle: llevar tres años aquí: Spanish's ultra-natural 'carry time' idiom for ongoing duration

hook.title: Carrying Time on Your Back: Llevo Tres Años Aquí
hook.content: Alongside Vivo aquí desde hace tres años, everyday Spanish has an even shorter, ultra-idiomatic way to express ongoing duration: use the verb llevar ('to carry / wear'): Llevo tres años aquí (literally 'I carry three years here' = 'I've been here for three years')!

pattern.title: Three Ways to Express Ongoing Duration
pattern.content:
1) Vivo aquí desde hace tres años.
2) Hace tres años que vivo aquí.
3) Llevo tres años aquí.
All three keep the verb in the PRESENT tense because the action is still going on!

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:

matching_pairs.english: I have lived here for three years (with desde hace)
matching_pairs.german: vivo aquí desde hace tres años

matching_pairs.english: I have been here for three years (lit. I carry three years here)

exercises.target_answer: vivo aquí desde hace tres años, llevo tres años aquí, desde hace dos semanas, desde el lunes
exercises.meaning: I have lived here for three years (with desde hace), I have been here for three years (lit. I carry three years here), for two weeks, since Monday
exercises.explanation: Both desde hace and llevar + time use the present tense for ongoing duration.

exercises.prompt: What does a native speaker in Madrid mean by 'Llevo dos años en Madrid'?
options: I left Madrid two years ago
I will go to Madrid in two years
I have been (living) in Madrid for two years
exercises.target_answer: I have been (living) in Madrid for two years
exercises.meaning: I have been in Madrid for two years
exercises.explanation: llevar + time span literally pictures 'carrying' the accumulated time you've spent somewhere!

exercises.prompt: Assemble: 'I have lived in this house for three years'
exercises.target_answer: Vivo en esta casa desde hace tres años
exercises.meaning: I have lived in this house for three years
exercises.explanation: Vivo en esta casa desde hace tres años.

exercises.prompt: Fold the indirect receiver into its Spanish dative pronoun:
exercises.full_sentence: Ella habla al médico por la mañana
exercises.explanation: The indirect receiver al médico folds into the pre-verbal dative clitic le: Ella le habla.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Vivo aquí desde hace diez años
exercises.target_answer: Vivo aquí desde hace diez años
exercises.meaning: I have lived here for ten years
exercises.explanation: Vivo aquí desde hace diez años.

summary.outcome: Recognize llevar + time and produce present-tense duration sentences with desde and desde hace.

use_example.german: Vivo en esta ciudad desde hace diez años.
use_example.english: I have lived in this city for ten years.

summary.takeaway: Spanish views ongoing duration as present reality (vivo / estoy / llevo).
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next ([21] Comparatives: más, menos, mejor): compare anything in Spanish with más, menos, mejor, peor, and tan... como!

twist.prompt: Assemble: 'I have been here for two weeks'
twist.target_answer: Estoy aquí desde hace dos semanas
twist.explanation: Estoy aquí desde hace dos semanas.

desde.context_phrase: Vivo aquí desde hace tres años.
desde.context_translation: I have lived here for three years.
desde.etymology_derivation: Just like French depuis, ongoing actions in Spanish stay in the PRESENT tense with desde hace (or hace X que + present)!

vivir.etymology_derivation: Latin vīvere — English vivid, revive, survive.

año.english_meaning: year (tener X años: to be X years old)
año.context_translation: I am thirty years old (lit. I have thirty years).
año.etymology_derivation: Latin double -nn- evolved into Spanish palatal ñ (written with a tilde, originally a tiny n drawn above the first n!).

semana.context_translation: This week I have a lot of work.

tres.etymology_derivation: Shared Indo-European root with English three.

ciudad.etymology_derivation: Latin cīvitātem ('citizenship, city') gives English 'city' and 'civic', and Spanish ciudad.
